targetCompanyImage.name: Vineyard Offshore
targetCompanyImage.description: Vineyard Offshore is Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners' U.S. offshore-wind development platform, established in 2022 with lease areas held through CI IV. Excelsior Wind is the current 1,350 MW New York project configuration within the broader Vineyard Mid-Atlantic federal lease and construction-and-operations-plan envelope, whose legal lessee is Vineyard Mid-Atlantic LLC. Excelsior is therefore a nested project and lease SPV history, not a second manager-level PortCo. The lease became effective in May 2022; New York provisionally selected an earlier 1,314 MW configuration in 2023, but no final award or executed offtake followed, and the later 1,350 MW bid received no award when the 2024 solicitation closed in February 2026. BOEM began environmental review in January 2025, and the project remains in development and uncontracted. No lease transfer, sale, relinquishment, CIP exit or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 19, 2026.

milestones.event: Federal lease OCS-A 0544 became effective for Vineyard Mid-Atlantic LLC, the lease SPV for the area containing Excelsior Wind.
BOEM issued its notice of intent to prepare an environmental impact statement for the broader Vineyard Mid-Atlantic project.
NYSERDA closed the 2024 offshore-wind solicitation without awards, leaving Excelsior's 1,350 MW bid uncontracted.
Public platform materials state that Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners-supported Vineyard Offshore was established in 2022 with initial lease areas owned by Copenhagen Infrastructure IV (CI IV).
Vineyard Offshore announced New York's provisional selection of an earlier Excelsior Wind configuration, but the round closed without a final award or executed offtake.
Vineyard Offshore announced Vineyard Northeast for New England.
